title: Classify Codex thread-store writer conflicts instead of dumping opaque stderr
body:
**Reproduced bug. Priority: P1.** Research at `6c7a6fbe`, 2026-09-06. Corrected after lead review. Live on the Codex lead at 06:31Z: worker finished, auto-continue ran `codex exec resume` for session `01a072f7-10e0-7fd2-b691-7d481327516f`, CLI died in under a second with `thread-store conflict: thread already has an active writer` (also reported as JSON-RPC -32600). Retry appeared. A second attempt one second later failed the same way. The user had to ask what the dump meant. The process holding that writer is unknown from this incident.

### Problem
Codex serializes writers per thread (openai/codex#37403, #37450). Solenta treats the failure as a generic nonzero exit. The transcript shows raw `codex_core::session` logs. Nothing names a writer conflict, says Retry can be used after the owner releases, or warns not to delete sessions. This issue does not claim the session bytes are known intact, and it does not name Desktop or any other process as the proven holder.

### Reproduction
1. Seed a Codex thread with a stored sessionId.
2. Have a worker finish so `flushOrchNotices` starts `codex exec resume <sessionId>`.
3. Make the fake CLI print the live writer-conflict stderr (explicit `thread-store conflict` / `already has an active writer` text) and exit 1. Do not use the user's Desktop or `~/.codex`.
4. Observe status failed, last event `Run error (exit 1):` plus the raw lock lines, `lastErrorKind` unset.
5. Retry turn re-sends that notice and immediately runs the same resume.

`classifyClaudeResultError` reports `sessionLost: false` for this stderr. `classifyContextOverflow` and `classifyCliUpgrade` return null. `looksSessionLost` only matches `No conversation found`.

### Cause
Codex `onExit` calls `formatRunExitError` then `markRunFailed`. Those paths know grok config corruption, context overflow, and CLI upgrade. They do not know thread-store writer conflicts, so the UI cannot offer a specific recovery.

### Smallest useful correction
- Classify only when the text explicitly includes writer-conflict wording such as `thread-store conflict` or `already has an active writer`. Do not treat generic JSON-RPC `-32600` alone as this class.
- Replace the dump with: Codex refused the resume because another writer holds this thread; Retry after that owner releases; do not delete sessions. Do not name a specific holder unless identified.
- Keep the raw CLI lines behind a detail, the way overflow already keeps a short provider excerpt.
- Keep `sessionId`. This is an exclusive-writer refusal, not a lost conversation.
- Do not permanently disable Retry from a stored `lastError`. After Codex accepts the session again, a manual Retry must still run. Immediate auto-retry of the same doomed resume is the loop to avoid, not Retry itself.

### Acceptance
The same fake-CLI fixture, whose stderr contains explicit writer-conflict text, fails with the recovery copy rather than a raw `codex_core` log. `lastErrorKind` is a stable writer-lock class only for that explicit text. A stderr of `-32600` without writer-conflict wording is not this class. `sessionId` is still present. A later manual Retry after the CLI accepts the session still resumes that id. A stale lastError does not block Retry by itself. Claude's `No conversation found` reset path is unchanged.

Related: #406 is agent-facing tool errors, not this user-visible CLI resume. #391 is agent same-fix thrash. #297 is CI flake taxonomy. #554 is the eject hatch to reuse. #795/#799 were argv bugs on `exec resume` and are closed; resume argv is already `exec resume <id>` without `--sandbox`.

Sources: [sessionLost is Claude-shaped](https://github.com/currentbits/solenta/blob/6c7a6fbebb066942f7f5702084f1af1e0730319d/electron/runner.js#L310), [generic exit copy](https://github.com/currentbits/solenta/blob/6c7a6fbebb066942f7f5702084f1af1e0730319d/electron/runner.js#L380), [Codex onExit](https://github.com/currentbits/solenta/blob/6c7a6fbebb066942f7f5702084f1af1e0730319d/electron/runner.js#L4871), [overflow/upgrade only](https://github.com/currentbits/solenta/blob/6c7a6fbebb066942f7f5702084f1af1e0730319d/electron/quotaWait.js#L76).

Evidence: `node --import=./test/support/disable-grok-mcp.mjs --experimental-strip-types docs/issue-drafts/2026-09-06-runtime-evidence.mjs` exits 0. Fake Codex binary and temp Store only. Did not spawn real Codex, kill Desktop, or delete `~/.codex/sessions`.

Requested disposition: keep OPEN Planboard issue, plan:todo. Research only; no app implementation.

title: Do not auto-continue a Codex lead while another process holds the session writer
body:
**Reproduced bug. Priority: P1.** Research at `6c7a6fbe`, 2026-09-06. Corrected after lead review. Same live incident as the writer-lock classification gap: a finished worker woke the idle Codex lead, Solenta spawned `exec resume` immediately, Codex refused with explicit writer-conflict text, and the crew stalled. The holder of that writer is unknown from this incident.

### Problem
`flushOrchNotices` delivers the worker-finished prompt as soon as Solenta's `active` map does not contain the lead. Codex's thread store is single-writer. Idle in Solenta is not the same as Codex accepting the resume. Possible holders include Desktop, another `codex` CLI, a previous Solenta child still shutting down, or a stale writer (openai/codex#37403 / #37450). This issue does not prove which one held the lock here.

### Reproduction
1. Codex lead with a stored sessionId, status done, not in `active`.
2. Simulate-provider worker flagged `orchWorker` finishes.
3. Lead auto-starts. Captured argv is `exec resume <sessionId>`.
4. Fake CLI exits 1 with explicit writer-conflict stderr. Lead is failed in well under a second.

Separately, `materializeCodexGuardrailHome` symlinks `sessions/` and `thread-writer-locks/` from the source Codex home (everything except `hooks.json`). That is shared locking on shared session data. The fixture proves the symlink exists; it is not evidence that the symlink is defective, and this ticket must not unlink or privatize the lock dir while sessions remain shared.

### Cause
The only skip in `flushOrchNotices` is `active.has(threadId)`. `startCodexRun` always passes `thread.sessionId` into `buildArgs`, which emits `exec resume`. Solenta then treats a writer-conflict exit as a generic failed turn and is ready to auto-continue or Retry immediately.

### Smallest useful correction
- On an explicit Codex writer-conflict rejection (same text class as #952), park the notice. Do not auto-start another `exec resume`.
- Optional short wait/retry (once, bounded) only when Solenta itself just released its own child and Codex then accepts. Do not busy-loop.
- After ownership is actually released (the CLI accepts the session), allow bounded auto-flush or a manual Retry to deliver the parked notice. Keep `sessionId`.
- Never delete, skip, or bypass Codex locks. Never treat a stored `lastError` as proof that a lock is still held.
- Preserve shared locking: sessions and writer locks stay in the same Codex home namespace. Do not recommend a private/unlinked lock dir beside shared sessions.
- Reuse eject (#554) if the user wants the raw CLI to own the session. Marking a thread ejected should prevent Solenta from resuming it.
- Do not start a second Solenta Codex child for the same sessionId while one is still in `active` or still shutting down.

### Acceptance
Worker-finished notice plus an explicit writer-conflict rejection does not spawn another auto `exec resume`. The notice stays parked with recovery copy. Overlay still shares `sessions/` and `thread-writer-locks/` with the source Codex home. After Codex accepts the session (not inferred from lastError), a bounded or manual retry delivers the notice and resumes. Claude/Grok auto-continue is unchanged. A user send still runs (existing budget/cap comment).

Related: pair with the writer-lock classification issue from this audit. #687 already preserves question cards on fromNotice; do not reopen it. #808 was workflow phase resume and is closed. #795/#799 were resume argv and are closed.

Sources: [flushOrchNotices](https://github.com/currentbits/solenta/blob/6c7a6fbebb066942f7f5702084f1af1e0730319d/electron/runner.js#L1176), [fromNotice startRun](https://github.com/currentbits/solenta/blob/6c7a6fbebb066942f7f5702084f1af1e0730319d/electron/runner.js#L1197), [Codex resume argv](https://github.com/currentbits/solenta/blob/6c7a6fbebb066942f7f5702084f1af1e0730319d/electron/providers.js#L379), [overlay symlink-all](https://github.com/currentbits/solenta/blob/6c7a6fbebb066942f7f5702084f1af1e0730319d/electron/codex-guardrail.js#L52).

Evidence: `node --import=./test/support/disable-grok-mcp.mjs --experimental-strip-types docs/issue-drafts/2026-09-06-runtime-evidence.mjs` exits 0. Fake Codex binary, temp overlay source, temp Store. Did not spawn real Codex, kill Desktop, or delete `~/.codex/sessions`.

Requested disposition: keep OPEN Planboard issue, plan:todo. Research only; no app implementation.

title: Retry turn after a failed machine-delivered notice re-sends the wrong prompt
body:
**Reproduced bug. Priority: P1.** Research at `6c7a6fbe`, 2026-09-06. Retry turn always re-sends `lastUserMessage` through the ordinary composer `onStartRun` path. That is the wrong prompt after an undeliverable orchestration notice, and the wrong turn class after a failed fromNotice spawn.

### Problem
`flushOrchNotices` already comments that refusing a wake-up in that function (not in `startRun`) lets "Retry turn after raising a cap" still run. Retry does not re-deliver the parked notice. It re-sends whatever user row is last.

Two current outcomes:

1. Undeliverable notice (daily budget, orchestration ceiling, missing CLI). The catch appends an event containing the notice and `Not delivered:`. No user row is added. Retry button title is the original user prompt. Clicking it starts a new human turn of that original task, not the worker-finished continue.
2. fromNotice spawn that fails after append (Codex writer-lock in the live incident). The notice is already a user row. Retry re-sends that notice, but as `fromNotice: false`, so it resets the auto-turn cap and still `exec resume`s immediately.

### Reproduction
Unit, using the real `lastUserMessage` / `retryAnchorEventId` helpers:
- Transcript `[original user, assistant, notice user, lock error event]` anchors Retry on the error and would send the notice text.
- Transcript `[original user, assistant, notice+Not delivered event]` anchors Retry on the error and would send `look at the app`.

Runner fixture: worker-finished auto-continue fails Codex resume; Retry `startRun(lastUser.text)` captures `exec resume` of the same sessionId and fails again. The existing electron test `an undeliverable wake-up lands the orchestrator failed` already shows the event-only path with zero user rows on a lead that never ran; a lead that already has its first prompt then retries that first prompt.

### Cause
`ThreadView` `handleRetry` calls `onStartRun(retryUser.text, undefined, retryUser.attachments)` with no fromNotice flag and no pointer at the failed run. `retryTurn.ts` documents that click re-sends the last user message via the Composer path.

### Smallest useful correction
- If the last event is a failed or undeliverable fromNotice, Retry should re-deliver that notice (same prompt, `fromNotice: true`), not the oldest leftover user row.
- If that notice failed as an explicit Codex writer-conflict, do not immediately auto-retry the same resume. After Codex accepts the session, a manual Retry must still work. Do not disable Retry from a stored lastError.
- Keep ordinary Retry of a human turn as last user message.
- After raising a budget/cap, Retry must deliver the parked notice, matching the existing `flushOrchNotices` comment.
- Tooltip should name the notice (`Retry: continue orchestrating`) rather than the original task when that is what will run.

### Acceptance
Undeliverable worker-finished notice: Retry after raising the cap delivers the notice, not the original user prompt. Failed fromNotice spawn: Retry re-delivers the notice; it does not immediately loop a writer-conflict resume, and it remains usable after Codex accepts the session. A later human prompt still retries that human prompt. Workflow-slot Retry (#830) is unchanged.

Related: #687 preserves question cards on machine turns; this is Retry prompt selection. #391 is agent thrash, not the Retry button. #830 closed workflow-slot routing.

Sources: [Retry click](https://github.com/currentbits/solenta/blob/6c7a6fbebb066942f7f5702084f1af1e0730319d/src/components/ThreadView.tsx#L4886), [last user message](https://github.com/currentbits/solenta/blob/6c7a6fbebb066942f7f5702084f1af1e0730319d/src/retryTurn.ts#L31), [fromNotice user append](https://github.com/currentbits/solenta/blob/6c7a6fbebb066942f7f5702084f1af1e0730319d/electron/runner.js#L7735), [undeliverable event](https://github.com/currentbits/solenta/blob/6c7a6fbebb066942f7f5702084f1af1e0730319d/electron/runner.js#L1206).

Evidence: `node --import=./test/support/disable-grok-mcp.mjs --experimental-strip-types docs/issue-drafts/2026-09-06-runtime-evidence.mjs` exits 0. Uses `retryTurn.ts` and a temp createRunner fixture. Did not spawn real Codex, kill Desktop, or delete `~/.codex/sessions`.

Requested disposition: keep OPEN Planboard issue, plan:todo. Research only; no app implementation.
